text:
Zeev Buium is 20, playing nearly 22 minutes a night, and lately closer to 24 since his role grew. That is a lot to ask of a defenseman who was one of the main pieces coming back when Vancouver traded Quinn Hughes to Minnesota. On Saturday he finally scored his first goal of the season, against the Wild.

The points (six in 25 games) sit right at the 0.24-a-game median for defensemen drafted around him in their first full season. The harder numbers are on the defensive side: the Canucks take 35.8% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey's note from last season says the same thing in a different way: opponents got more chances with him out there (bottom 7% of defensemen), and his teammates were weak, which makes the raw numbers look worse than his own effect.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows what he's for. He carries the puck in on 46% of his entries, and 28% of his shots come off the rush (typical 17%). The Province asked how he "measures progress when points vanish"; at 20, minutes like these are the progress.
